cards.label: Model answer 2 of 3
cards.title: Index of refraction
cards.body: The index of refraction is the ratio of the speed in vacuum to the speed in the medium, \(n = c/v\). Since \(\varepsilon = \varepsilon_r\varepsilon_0\) and \(\mu = \mu_r\mu_0\), this gives \(n = \sqrt{\varepsilon_r\mu_r}\).

cards.label: Model answer 5 of 6
cards.title: Reflection and transmission coefficients
cards.body: The reflection coefficient is \(R = ((1-\beta)/(1+\beta))^2\) and the transmission coefficient is \(T = 4\beta/(1+\beta)^2\). With equal permeabilities \(\beta = n_2/n_1\), so \(R = ((n_1-n_2)/(n_1+n_2))^2\) and \(T = 4n_1n_2/(n_1+n_2)^2\).

cards.label: Model answer 6 of 6
cards.title: Check R + T = 1
cards.body: Adding the two coefficients, \((1-\beta)^2 + 4\beta = (1+\beta)^2\), so \(R + T = 1\). Energy is conserved at the boundary: the reflected and transmitted intensities together equal the incident intensity.

cards.title: Meaning of the time constant
cards.body: The time constant is \(\tau = L/R\). At \(t = \tau\), \(i = I_0(1 - e^{-1}) = 0.632\,I_0\), so the current has reached 63.2 percent of its final value. A larger \(L/R\) means a longer time constant.

cards.title: Initial slope and final value
cards.body: At \(t = 0\) the current is zero, so the initial rate of growth is \(di/dt = V/L\). As \(t\) becomes large the current approaches the final value \(I_0 = V/R\), where the rate of growth is zero.
